stem:
Match column I with column II and select the correct option from the given codes.

(Column I shows micrographs of three types of white blood cells: (a) a cell with a large bilobed/multilobed nucleus and fine granules — a neutrophil; (b) a cell almost filled by a single large rounded dark-staining nucleus with few granules — a basophil; (c) a cell with a curved nucleus and prominent coarse granules — an eosinophil. Column II lists their functions.)

| Column I | Column II |
|---|---|
| (a) bilobed-nucleus granulocyte (neutrophil) | (i) Phagocytosis |
| (b) cell with a large rounded nucleus, few granules (basophil) | (ii) Release heparin |
| (c) coarse-granuled cell with curved nucleus (eosinophil) | (iii) Allergic response |

Which of the following epithelial tissues lines the stomach and intestine?

(The four options are diagrams of epithelial tissue types. Option a: a single row of tall, column-shaped cells with nuclei near the base and a brush border on top — columnar epithelium. Option b: a single layer of squat, cube-shaped cells each with a central nucleus — cuboidal epithelium. Option c: a basal layer of tall cells topped by flattened layered cells — stratified epithelium. Option d: a sheet of flat, irregular, polygonal cells seen in surface view — squamous epithelium.)

options.label: A
options.text: Columnar epithelium (tall column-shaped cells with basal nuclei)

options.label: B
options.text: Cuboidal epithelium (single layer of cube-shaped cells)

options.label: D
options.text: Squamous epithelium (flat polygonal cells in surface view)

stem:
While observing a thin section of a plant stem, four students sketched sclerenchyma as given below. The correct diagram is:

(Four sketches A, B, C, D of plant cells. A: a single broad cell with thin walls, a large lumen and a visible nucleus. B: cells with somewhat thickened walls that still contain living nuclei. C: long, narrow cells with very thick lignified walls, a very narrow lumen and tapering pointed ends and no living contents. D: cells with thick walls bearing pits/dots and a narrow lumen with blunt ends.)

options.label: A
options.text: C (long narrow cells, very thick lignified walls, narrow lumen, pointed ends)

options.label: B
options.text: B (cells with thickened walls and living nuclei)

options.label: C
options.text: A (broad thin-walled cell with large lumen and nucleus)

options.label: D
options.text: D (thick-walled cells with pits and blunt ends)

stem:
Which one of the following diagrams represents the correct observation of a human cheek cell under a compound microscope?

(Four sketches A, B, C, D. A: loosely arranged rounded/irregular cells without thick walls, each with a single nucleus — the membrane-bound shape of cheek cells. B: angular hexagonal cells with thick rigid walls and a dot nucleus — a plant-tissue appearance. C: rounded cells, each with a single dense dark-stained nucleus. D: empty hexagonal thick-walled cells — a plant-tissue appearance.)

options.label: A
options.text: B (angular hexagonal cells with thick walls)

options.label: B
options.text: A (rounded membrane-bound cells, no cell wall, single nucleus)

options.label: D
options.text: C (rounded cells with dense dark nuclei)

stem:
Given below is the diagram showing the structure of a Parenchyma cell. Which marking are wrong?

(The figure shows a cluster of rounded parenchyma cells with label arrows reading, from top to bottom: Cell membrane, Cytoplasm, Intercellular space, Cell wall, Nucleus. The arrow labelled 'Intercellular space' points into the interior of a cell rather than to the gap between adjacent cells, and the arrow labelled 'Cytoplasm' does not point to the granular interior.)

Which type of muscles are shown in the image?

(The figure shows long, spindle-shaped muscle cells, each tapering at both ends with a single central nucleus and no cross-striations — smooth/unstriated muscle.)

options.label: C
options.text: Both Spindle - shaped, uninucleated and Elongated, without striations

stem:
When an onion peel cell is placed in a hypertonic solution, it will look like?

(Four sketches A, B, C, D of an onion epidermal cell. A: a cell with a star-like spiky outline and a central nucleus. B: a fully turgid cell whose protoplasm presses against and fills the rectangular cell wall. C: a cell whose protoplasm has begun to detach at one corner. D: a cell whose protoplasm has shrunk into a small rounded mass pulled completely away from the cell wall, with strands connecting it to the wall — full plasmolysis.)

options.label: A
options.text: D (protoplasm shrunk and pulled away from the cell wall — plasmolysed)

options.label: B
options.text: B (turgid cell, protoplasm filling the cell wall)

options.label: C
options.text: C (protoplasm detached only at one corner)

options.label: D
options.text: A (cell with a star-shaped spiky outline)

stem:
The type of blood cell represented by 'A' is:

(The figure shows blood corpuscles: neutrophil, eosinophil, basophil, lymphocyte and monocyte are bracketed together and labelled 'A', while platelets are shown separately to the side. The bracket 'A' encloses all the nucleated leucocytes.)

On observing a permanent slide under the microscope a student found the structure without cell wall. It had light and dark bands. The slide could be:

(The figure shows an elongated cylindrical muscle fibre marked with alternating light bands and dark bands across its length, with a nucleus indicated — cross-striations of a striated muscle.)

The student were shown the slide of a nerve cell. They were asked to drawn the diagram of the nerve cell. The correct sequence of the labelling 1, 2, 3, 4 is:

(The figure shows a neuron with four label arrows. Label 1 points to a short, branched process arising from the cell body; label 2 points to the cell body region around the nucleus; label 3 points to the dark central nucleus; label 4 points to the single long, slender process extending away from the cell body.)

X, Y and Z are meristematic tissues present at different regions in plants. Which of these are responsible for the increase in girth of stems or roots?

(The figure shows a young plant. X labels the growing tip at the shoot apex; Y labels a region at a node between the internodes; Z labels the lateral region along the lower part of the stem near the root.)

The tissue shown is found in:

(The figure shows branched, cylindrical, striated muscle fibres joined end to end by intercalated discs, each fibre having a single central nucleus — cardiac muscle.)

Identify the plant tissue on the basis of distinguishing features shown in the given image.

(The figure shows a group of thick-walled cells labelled with a lignified secondary wall, an empty lumen with no living content, and a simple pit — the features of sclerenchyma.)

The image shows a muscular tissue found attached to the bones and help in the body movements. Identify.

(The figure shows a long, cylindrical, unbranched muscle fibre with prominent cross-striations and several nuclei arranged along its periphery — striated/skeletal muscle.)

Four students marked an onion epidermal cell seen under high power microscope as below. Identify the correctly labelled diagram:

(Four sketches A, B, C, D of an onion epidermal cell, each with four label arrows. A: Cell wall -> outer boundary, Vacuole -> large central space, Cytoplasm -> thin granular lining, Nucleus -> small body at the edge (all correct). B: labels read Cell wall, Cytoplasm, Vacuole, Nucleus (cytoplasm and vacuole order swapped). C: labels read Cell wall, Nucleus, Vacuole, Cytoplasm (wrongly ordered). D: labels read Cell wall, Vacuole, Cytoplasm, Nucleus but the arrows point to the wrong structures.)

options.label: A
options.text: A (Cell wall, Vacuole, Cytoplasm, Nucleus all correctly placed)

options.label: B
options.text: D (correct labels but arrows on wrong structures)

options.label: D
options.text: C (nucleus, vacuole and cytoplasm wrongly ordered)

stem:
Identify a connective tissue found around blood vessels and nerves and in the bone marrow.

(The figure shows a loose connective tissue with a matrix containing reticular fibres, collagen fibres, fibroblasts, macrophages, mast cells and plasma cells loosely scattered — areolar tissue.)

Identify the tissues in the given diagrams and choose the correct sequence.

(Four sketches labelled A, B, C, D. A: a regular network of hexagonal cells with uniformly thick walls and a large empty lumen — dead thick-walled cells. B: cells with dense, heavily thickened walls. C: loosely arranged rounded/irregular cells scattered with single nuclei and intercellular spaces. D: elongated rectangular brick-like cells arranged in a continuous sheet with nuclei.)

options.label: A
options.text: A : Sclerenchyma, B : Parenchyma, C : Cheek cells, D : Onion Peel

options.label: B
options.text: A : Sclerenchyma, B : Parenchyma, C : Onion peel, D : Cheek cells

options.label: C
options.text: A : Parenchyma, B : Sclerenchyma, C : Cheek cells, D : Onion peel

options.label: D
options.text: A : Parenchyma, B : Sclerenchyma, C : Onion peel, D : Cheek cells
